extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants interacting with KIPO (Korean IP Office)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for classification, publication (laying open), requests for examination, start and deferral of examination, and processing deadlines under KIPO practice. Targets how to classify inventions, when/how applications are published, and how examiners should proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC identification formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use typographic styles to indicate different kinds of IPC information: boldface type for invention information, regular (non-bold) type for additional information, italic style for extension level, and indexing code used only for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated styles for clarity in IPC identification; version/directive year-and-month indicated in square brackets; indexing code is used only for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional information (indexing codes or classification symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information is optional and may complement invention information; it can be given by either an indexing code or classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes are designated based on an indexing classification table categorized by technical functions (purpose, use, structure, material, manufacturing process, disposal process, control measure, etc.) not included in the classification place. After designating a classification symbol, an indexing code may be designated additionally for technical subject-matter useful to search.

rubrics_metrics.name: State national security confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention described in the specification must be confidential due to national security, that requirement shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part VII, chapter 3 for details; such matters are excluded from laying open/publication where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification inheritance for related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisional, converted, domestic priority claim, treaty priority claim, or application of lawful holder of right, the classification of the original application should be identified first and generally retained as the main classification of the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where original classifications obviously fail to correspond to the later application, prefer to keep the original classification as main and designate newly granted classification as sub-classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose classification place by apparatus/method/product hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle use the classification place for an apparatus or a method if a pertinent place exists; if the apparatus has no place use the method place; if the method has no place use the apparatus place; if neither exists, use the place for the product manufactured with the apparatus or method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply fallbacks in order: apparatus ↔ method ↔ product, so that the most pertinent available place is selected for accurate classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product classification: intrinsic → function → use
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufactured products shall be classified in the place pertinent to the product; if no such place exists, use an appropriate function-oriented place; if none exists, classify based on the use of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer intrinsic product characteristics; only resort to function or use when intrinsic classification place is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of multistage processes or plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A multistage process or plant consisting of multiple stages or apparatuses shall be classified with the place pertinent to the composition; if no such classification place exists, use the place for the output produced by the composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where constituents have individual characteristics, classify each constituent with its classification place as well. If composition has no intrinsic characteristics but constituents do, do not classify the composition itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of specifics or structural parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural or functional specifics or parts are used only for a certain apparatus, classify the claimed invention into the place for that apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such specifics or parts can be used for more than two apparatuses, classify into the place for the specifics/parts; if no place exists for them, classify in place for the relevant apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when subject matter spans multiple groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a single technical subject-matter is related directly and intrinsically to more than two groups, classify it into the place for all related groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject-matter is included in more than two groups of equal level under the same main group, classify into the place for a higher hierarchical group. However, if inclusion in multiple groups is of little importance for search and the matter is simply relevant to a combination of elements, excess multiple-group classification may be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of chemical compounds (Section C principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical compounds (organic, inorganic, polymer) shall be classified in the relevant place for Section C according to intrinsic characteristics (chemical structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the compound is also related to a field of use and that field is essential content of the technical subject-matter, classify the field of use if a pertinent place exists. If the subject-matter is related only to the use of the compound, classify only the field of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of mixtures or compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixtures or compositions in the claimed invention shall be classified into the relevant place pursuant to their intrinsic features (e.g., C03C for glass composition, C04B for cement/ceramic composition, C22C for alloy composition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no relevant place exists for the mixture/composition, classify pursuant to their use or application. If essential characteristics are in the use/application, classify both the mixture/composition per se and their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of manufacture or treatment of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimed invention relates to manufacture or treatment of compounds, the compounds per se shall be classified; methods of manufacture or treatment shall also be classified if pertinent places exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General methods for manufacture/treatment of compounds should be classified in the relevant place if such place exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification for Markush-type compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush-type chemical compounds generally defined in a chemical formula, classify the general chemical formula individually if it has few relevant places (for example, less than 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specified compounds are things per se in the claims (composition), outputs from claimed processes, or derivatives, classify the compounds in each relevant place. 'Specified' includes being designated by formula/title, inferred from specific reactants, identified by physical properties, or described with detailed manufacturing examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification for combinatorial libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: For combinatorial libraries involving many compounds or biological entities, assign IPC to each individual compound as for Markush-type classification; classify characteristics of the entire library into combinatorial chemistry (C40B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat individual members like Markush entries; the library as a whole gets a combinatorial-chemistry classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC structure: main trunk, indexing codes (2000 series), Section Y
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC is divided into Main trunk, Indexing codes (2000 series), and Section Y; indexing codes provide additional information and are attached only to additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes (2000-series) are optional classification elements and not obligatory unless extra direction exists in the main trunk or its definition. ICO-style groups include breakdown indexing codes and orthogonal indexing codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC main trunk correspondence and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPC main trunk has an IPC classification place corresponding to it, the CPC title is generally the same as the IPC's; information added only in CPC (no IPC correspondence) is indicated in braces { }. CPC subgroup numbers allow finer breakdown than IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CPC's added detail when IPC lacks a corresponding place; recognize { } notation as CPC-only content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy indicated by indentation/dots in CPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Hierarchy among CPC subgroups is determined by the number of dots preceding each title; indentation (number of dots) indicates subgroup level rather than subgroup digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret subgroup hierarchy by indentation: one-dot subgroup is higher level than two-dots subgroup even if both have two-digit numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual subclass/group usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual subclasses or residual main groups are used for technology not categorized elsewhere; their titles typically express 'not included in any other group.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to residual groups only when subject matter genuinely does not fit other categories (e.g., F21K residual subclass examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of laying open (publication) of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Laying open of applications publishes applications after a prescribed period to prevent overlap in investment and research and to make inventions available as technical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laying open separates publication from examination to avoid delays in making prior art available even if examination is slow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for laying open (18 months rule and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be laid open after one year and six months from the filing date; for priority-claiming applications the period starts from filing date of first application (or earliest filing date if multiple priorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional/converted applications are deemed filed on parent filing date so the laying-open period follows the parent filing date; early publication can be requested via prescribed form to lay open earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications excluded from laying open
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applications are excluded from being laid open: those without claims as prescribed, those whose registration is published, or applications invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or decided to be rejected. Also excluded are applications containing matters requiring confidentiality for national security, contravening public order/morality, or harming public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exclusions per Article 19(3) Enforcement Decree and Patent Act Article 64; examples include prior-filed applications used for domestic priority claims under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of laying open (rights and prior art status)
rubrics_metrics.description: After laying open, the applicant may warn persons practicing the invention and claim compensation for use after the date of warning or when the person knew of the laid-open application; however, compensation cannot be exercised until patent registration is established. Laid-open application becomes prior art and may be used against later applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning and compensation are inchoate rights pending registration; the laid-open application is citable as prior art pursuant to Patent Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination must be made only for an application pending in KIPO, only once per application, and within three years from filing date (five years for applications filed on or before 2017-02-28); divisional/converted applications have special 30-day windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-language applications require Korean translation attached; international applications must request examination within three years from international filing date; failure to request within the period deems the application withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request examination and formality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (including third parties without interest) may request examination; incompetent persons must act via legal representative; associations/foundations without juridical person status may file via designated representative/administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requestors must submit the prescribed form and pay examination fee; once admitted the request cannot be withdrawn; valid request survives loss of legal capacity (e.g., death).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and increased claims after examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: When the number of claims increases due to amendments after a third-party request for examination, the applicant must pay additional examination fees corresponding to the increased claims; failure to pay can result in instruction to pay and possible invalidation of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional fees are not paid as requested, amendments may be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of filing a request for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for which examination is requested will be examined; pendency is terminated only by patent registration or rejection (unless invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned). The purpose of an early request is published with the application if the request was made before laying open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request is filed by a third party, KIPO notifies the applicant; exam decisions (including withdrawal/abandonment) are notified to the third party who requested examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's pre-examination verifications and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting examination, the examiner shall verify whether the application is classified appropriately per CPC/IPC and whether it falls within the examiner's classification responsibility; if misallocated, reallocation or correction should be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allocated to wrong classification, reallocate to correct examiner after consultation; if reallocation not made properly, ask Patent Examination Policy Division to correct classification and reassign the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner disqualification and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must assess whether disqualification reasons under Article 148 (subparagraphs listed) apply or if they should be excluded due to recent employment at an applicant's organization; if disqualified, transfer the application to another examiner in the most similar technical classification with approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider conflicts of interest including recent employment (less than 2 years as examiner but worked at applicant organization in the last 3 years before appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination and priority rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination starts in order of requests per examiner or classification; priority is given to patent applications over utility model registrations when request dates are identical; among same-kind applications earlier filing date has priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional/converted applications are examined in request order, but may follow parent application order in certain circumstances (e.g., when filed after parent examination request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases permitting deferral of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may defer examination where: (i) a prior-filed or conflicting application is not laid open or not requested for examination; (ii) a prior-filed domestic priority application is prior to withdrawal period under Article 56; (iii) related trial or litigation is pending; (iv) search is outsourced or outside specialist advice/consultation required; (v) period for submitting evidential priority documents has not elapsed; (vi) other needs for deferment arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part 5 Chapter 3 for detailed deferment and pendency extension provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines for specific examination actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set timeframes: examiner to begin reexamination remand cases within one month of receipt (report reasons if unavoidable); expedited examination category determination within 7 days and start of examination within 2 months from delivery of notice (4 months for certain expedited categories); other deadlines tabulated (e.g., 15 days, 1 month, 2 months, 3 months) for prior-art search requests, amendment periods, resume after remand, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Instruction Articles cited (e.g., Instruction Article 59, Article 86, Article 66) and the provided table for accurate initial dates and times for each type of processing deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for law application (transitional measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Patent Act is revised while an application is pending, transitional measures prevent disadvantages: provisions of law shall be applied as of the filing date. Divisional/converted applications and applications filed by lawful right holders are deemed filed on the parent filing date so laws apply as of parent filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the legal regime in force as of the relevant filing date to avoid disadvantaging pending applications (examples provided).
